summary: Choose a running mate: You need a running mate, and the list is {rival}, who attacked you in the primary, {loyal ally}, who backed you early, and {safe pick}.
realLife: One life: In 2004 he picked John Edwards, who had called him a Washington insider in the primary. A campaign adviser later wrote that Kerry wished he had not. Another: In 2016 he chose Mike Pence, who had backed Ted Cruz in the primary, over finalists including Chris Christie. Another: Passed over for the 2016 ticket, he said the bridge scandal was a factor. Trump named him to lead the transition, then replaced him.
gates: You are your party's nominee for an office that has a running mate.
weights: What each brings in votes and money.

branches.then: They campaign well. Years later you wish you had not, when their secret comes out (C22).
They say a scandal on their record cost them. You put them in charge of your transition and remove them later (C44).

branches.then: They calm the party. Years later they are the one who must preside over your loss (C26).
